dedupe_keys.name: rio camboriu water producer programme brazil return on investment in watershed conservation tnc

description: This case study measures the return on investment of a payment for watershed services programme in the Camboriú River watershed in Santa Catarina, Brazil, whose main funder, the municipal water company EMASA, wants less suspended sediment at its drinking water intake. Timm Kroeger, Claudio Klemz, Daniel Shemie and co-authors from The Nature Conservancy and Brazilian partners set out a best-practice framework linking ecosystem service and benefit production functions with valuation and with-and-without scenarios. They project land use change without the programme from high-resolution imagery, calibrate a hydrologic model on flow and turbidity data, and value sediment reduction with treatment plant costs. Savings offset 80% of EMASA's investment and 60% of total costs over 2015 to 2045, so ROI is below 1 for sediment alone, while a tiny water surcharge would lift it above 1. Coverage is one Atlantic Forest watershed. Format and access: a 50-page TNC report and a journal article. Licence: not stated; free. Caveats: flood and water shortage co-benefits were not valued. It informs investment in natural infrastructure for water supply. Related catalogue records are the InVEST model and the Vittel ecosystem services case.

name: Rio Camboriú Water Producer programme, Brazil: return on investment in watershed conservation (TNC)
outcomes: Lower sediment treatment costs and water losses offset 80% of the water company's investment and 60% of total programme costs over 30 years, so ROI for sediment alone is below 1 (above 1 for the utility after 43 years); a surcharge of about USD 0.005 per cubic metre would lift ROI above 1, and flood and supply co-benefits were not monetised.
